insider_note: Each half needs three facts: the path, whether membranes are crossed, and the speed. Miss the membrane and the two halves stop being different.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Apoplast
steps.margin_note: Path, no membrane, fast. Four lines.
lines: The apoplast is the path of water transport in
a plant that does NOT cross any membrane.
Water moves through cell walls and the spaces
steps.why: Nothing has to be crossed, so the water is never slowed by a membrane — which is the whole reason this route is the fast one.
common_mistakes: Saying the apoplast crosses membranes. It does NOT; that is the symplast.
Calling the apoplast slow. It is the FASTER of the two paths.
steps.memory_tip: Apoplast is the outside lane: walls and gaps, no membranes, fast.

steps.label: Symplast
steps.margin_note: Mirror the apoplast lines: path, membranes crossed, slow.

lines.text: Apoplast goes around cells, symplast through

lines: The symplast is the path of water transport in
a plant that DOES cross membranes.
Water moves through the living cytoplasm, from
steps.why: Every membrane crossed costs time, so the route through the living cytoplasm is necessarily the slower one.
common_mistakes: Saying the symplast is the wall route. That is the apoplast.
Leaving out the speed. Fast against slow is half the contrast.
steps.memory_tip: Symplast is the inside lane: through the living cells, so slow.
